candidates.exact_span: Input pollutant geometric mean concentration as micro-gram per liter (ug/l or ppb) unless other unit is specified for the parameter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the applicable enforceable limit is compared against a geometric mean versus another aggregation, and whether units are ug/l/ppb or parameter-specific units, changes which numeric limit applies and whether a reported measurement exceeds it.

candidates.locator: Page 24, Section fact_sheet, STEP 2 data input
candidates.exact_span: Effluent value reported as "< detection level" (DL) but the DL is greater than MQL, input "1/2 DL" for calculation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Substituting one-half the detection limit when DL exceeds MQL yields a numeric value for limit comparison instead of a non-detect or missing result; a different reading of DL versus MQL or of the half-DL substitution rule changes whether Purpose A finds an exceedance and whether Purpose C classifies the result as a computed surrogate versus missing or non-comparable evidence.

candidates.locator: Page 24, Section fact_sheet, STEP 2 data input
candidates.exact_span: Effluent value reported as "< detection level" (DL) and the DL is smaller than MQL, no data is inputted.
candidates.computation_change_reason: When DL is below MQL, treating the value as no data removes it from numeric compliance comparison; interpreting DL, MQL, or the no-input rule differently changes whether Purpose A applies a limit at all and whether Purpose C records documented no-data versus a value eligible for comparison.

candidates.locator: Page 24, Section fact_sheet, STEP 2 data input
candidates.exact_span: If a less than MQL vakue is reported, input either the reported value or "0" for calculation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The disjunctive instruction to use either the reported less-than-MQL value or zero is ambiguous; choosing zero versus the reported value changes the numeric basis for limit comparison in Purpose A and whether Purpose C treats the period as evidenced by a zero/near-zero result versus unresolved or conditionally non-required monitoring.

Instream waste concentration derived from this formula can determine the operative numeric discharge or receiving-water limit; different interpretation of the formula or its inputs changes which enforceable limit applies and whether reported measurements exceed it.

candidates.locator: Page 24, Section fact_sheet, STEP 2 formula definitions
candidates.exact_span: F = Fraction of stream allow ed for mixing (see "Procedures for Implementing NPDES Permits in New Mexico")
candidates.computation_change_reason: The mixing fraction F is a direct input to Cd calculation; a different assigned or interpreted value for F changes the calculated instream concentration and thus the applicable numeric limit and exceedance determination.

candidates.locator: Page 24, Section fact_sheet, STEP 2 formula definitions
candidates.exact_span: Qa = Critical low flow of stream at discharge point expressed as the 4Q3 or harmonic mean flow for human health criteria
candidates.computation_change_reason: Selecting 4Q3 versus harmonic mean flow for Qa changes the denominator and numerator weighting in the Cd formula, which can change the derived applicable limit and whether measured concentrations are found to exceed it.

candidates.exact_span: TSS = Total suspended solids concentration found in receiving stream (or in effluent for intermittent stream)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The rule chooses receiving-stream versus effluent TSS for intermittent streams; using a different TSS source changes Kp and the dissolved metal limit derived from total criteria.
